reason: Both conversations missed the single most useful step - checking or swapping the fuse in the fused spur - and never asked about the door latch, and both leaned on the unsupported 'mains input module or control board' guess before escalating to an engineer. Conversation 1 wasted a turn asking the homeowner to plug a lamp into a switched spur that has no socket, pushed a model-number panel framed around 'a suitable replacement', and closed with a vaguer summary ('most likely on'). Conversation 2 was slightly more efficient and safety-conscious (don't keep resetting trips, don't remove panels, only check visible switches) and was explicitly honest that it was not recommending any part, which better matches the 'not-justified' part position; its only clear shortfall versus 1 is never collecting the make/model.
